learningObjective: Set up a public or internal Standard load balancer with a frontend, backend pool, health probe and rules, and fix load balancing problems.
engineer: The parts: frontend IP, the address clients connect to; backend pool, the VMs' network cards (NICs) or IP addresses (all in one VNet); health probe, which checks each VM (TCP, HTTP or HTTPS, every few seconds); load-balancing rule, which sends a frontend port to a backend port; inbound NAT rule, which forwards one port to one VM; outbound rule, for outbound internet.
Session persistence (on the rule): None, the default, which spreads by 5-tuple; Client IP, so the same client always goes to the same VM; Client IP and protocol.
SKU: Standard only (Basic was retired on 30 September 2025). Standard can be zone-redundant or zonal, gives detailed metrics, and supports HA ports on internal load balancers.
Standard is closed by default: the backend VMs' NSGs must allow the client traffic.

Health probes come from 168.63.129.16 (service tag AzureLoadBalancer). The default NSG rule AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound allows them. Your own deny rule with a lower number can block them. A VM that fails the probe gets no new connections.

Checking problems: the Health Probe Status and Data Path Availability metrics; Load Balancer Insights; the app listens on the probe port and path (an HTTP probe needs a 200 reply); the OS firewall; NSGs; the VM is in the backend pool.
A known limit: a backend VM can't call its own internal load balancer's frontend and land on itself.
Other load balancers: Application Gateway for layer 7 (URL paths, TLS, WAF); Front Door for global HTTP; Traffic Manager for global routing using DNS.

example.title: Three web servers across zones
body: A zone-redundant public Standard load balancer sits in front of three VMs in zones 1, 2 and 3, with an HTTP probe on /health. During patching, one VM fails the probe and is taken out automatically. Users don't notice.
An internal load balancer with HA ports sits in front of the SQL tier, for the availability group listener.

architectureDecisions: Probe a health page: an HTTP probe on an endpoint that lightly checks the app's dependencies.
Predictable outbound: use a NAT gateway or outbound rules.

misconceptions.myth: Load Balancer can route by URL path.
misconceptions.reality: No. It works at layer 4 (IP and port). Use Application Gateway for paths.

misconceptions.myth: A Standard load balancer lets traffic in without NSGs.
misconceptions.reality: No. Standard is closed by default. NSGs must allow the traffic.

comparisons.difference: Layer 7, in one region, with URL path routing, TLS and a web application firewall.
AWS's layer 4 load balancer. The AWS Application Load Balancer is layer 7.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong probe port or path, the app is down, or an NSG or OS firewall blocks 168.63.129.16.
troubleshooting.fix: Fix the probe, allow AzureLoadBalancer, and check the app returns 200.

troubleshooting.symptom: Clients time out on a public Standard load balancer.
troubleshooting.cause: The backend NSG doesn't allow the client traffic.

troubleshooting.symptom: Traffic always goes to one VM.
troubleshooting.cause: Session persistence is Client IP and there are few clients, or the other VMs are unhealthy.
troubleshooting.fix: Check probe status and the persistence setting.

troubleshooting.symptom: A backend VM can't reach the internal load balancer's frontend.
troubleshooting.cause: A backend VM calling its own frontend isn't supported.
troubleshooting.fix: Call the service directly, or test from a separate client VM.

configuration.limits: Backend pool members must be in one VNet
HA ports only on internal Standard load balancers
configuration.permissions: Network Contributor on the resource group
